messages:
alex: Customer Z reporting streaming response truncates mid-token — client sees HTTP/200 then socket close, no SSE `event: done` or final token. Happened in us-west-2, model=gpt-x, session_id=abc123. They attached pcap. @mira can you triage?

mira: ACK. any req_id / trace id?

alex: req_id=req_2035001234_abc123 trace=tr-7d9f; customer says it consistently fails ~18s after stream start. They also reported duplicate charges for the same chat session. Pcap link: s3://redwood-cs/pcaps/2035001234_customerZ.pcap

jon: FYI saw similar symptom in a different ticket — env/ALB idle-timeouts historically can cause abrupt closes. But 18s is shorter than typical 60s. Need server logs + tcpdump to confirm who sent FIN/RST.

priya: Customer note: mobile app (android) on cellular, aggressive reconnect. They included app-side pcap too.

mira: pulling logs for req_id... pasted snippet: ```
[2035001234.235] sse: stream_opened req=req_2035001234_abc123 trace=tr-7d9f
[2035001234.410] sse: chunk_sent bytes=256 seq=1
[2035001234.560] sse: chunk_sent bytes=512 seq=2
[2035001234.602] sse: connection_closed reason=early_eof sent_bytes=768
[2035001234.605] resume: token=077a... ttl_remaining=0 auth=ok
[2035001234.606] resume: resume_attempt req=req_2035001234_abc123_resume token=077a... -> 401
```

mira: resume token ttl_remaining=0 is suspicious — server thinks token expired immediately. If client reconnects quickly and token invalid, they get 401 and create a new session, which triggers billing again.

elena: deploy-bot: canary redeploy completed (rev=2026.3.20-canary) at 2035001225. That deploy included a change to envoy idle timeout (30s) + proxy keepalive handling. Could be related.

jon: tcpdump from edge shows sequence: server sends bytes until ~2035001234.602 then a FIN from server IP, no FIN from client. NAT gateway logs next show ephemeral port closed. Sample tcpdump lines: ```
12:34:56.010 IP server > client: seq=1 ack=1 len=512 PSH, ACK
12:34:56.048 IP server > client: seq=513 ack=1 len=256 PSH, ACK
12:34:56.102 IP server > client: FIN, ACK
```

jon: That indicates server closed socket. Need stack trace why server decided to close mid-stream. Could be internal quota, kv cache eviction, or a runtime guard triggered by a model kernel OOM fallback.

mira: Found a correlating runtime log earlier: ```
[2035001234.598] runtime: kvcache_lookup failed key=session_abc123 reason=evicted
[2035001234.599] runtime: model_streamer: detected client disconnect -> abort stream
```

mira: hypothesis: kv cache eviction caused server to decide stream invalid and close socket instead of sending a resume-friendly message. Combined with recent envoy change, resume token TTL logic may also be mis-set to zero on issuance, so client gets token that is unusable.

alex: Customer also shows duplicate billing: they reconnected after 401 and started a fresh session; billing records show two charge events within 5s.

priya: Customer asks for workaround while we triage.

mira: Immediate mitigations (short-term):
- send periodic SSE comments `: keepalive\n\n` every 10s to keep proxies/NAT alive and give mobile clients a visible heartbeat
- change resume token TTL to 60s (server-side config) so quick reconnects can resume
- on resume 401, respond with a JSON SSE event `event: resume_failed` with reason to avoid silent billing duplication
- add idempotency token check on start requests for billing dedupe

jon: Technical notes to reproduce locally: use curl with --no-buffer and an artificial slow network to mimic cellular:```bash
# reproduce
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-x" --max-time 120
```
NodeJS minimal repro (client reconnect logic):```js
const http = require('http')
const req = http.request({method:'GET', headers:{Accept:'text/event-stream', Authorization:'Bearer '+process.env.TK}}, res=>{
  res.on('data', chunk=>console.log('chunk', chunk.toString()))
  res.on('end', ()=>console.log('end'))
})
req.end()
```

mira: quick server config diff I propose: ```yaml
sse_keepalive_interval: 10000  # send comment lines every 10s
resume_token_ttl: 60s
resume_auth_on_resume: return_event_on_failure
billing: idempotency_window: 10s
```

elena: will open a release PR with the keepalive + resume_ttl patch and target a small canary run on staging and one host in prod. link: https://git.redwood.dev/repo/pulls/1248

mira: also adding a short-term observability improvement: emit `sse.close_reason` tag + resume_token_issued_at in tracing so we can correlate.

support-bot: created incident INC-2035001 "streaming truncation & resume failures - customer Z" and assigned to eng-runtime team.

alex: I'll reply to customer with: 1) workaround — update mobile SDK to handle SSE comments as heartbeat and delay duplicate start for 15s; 2) we're scheduling a canary with keepalive + resume TTL changes and will follow up when canary completes. :pray:

priya: Customer agreed to test a canary build later today. Also requested that we avoid breaking other customers — please keep rollout gradual.

mira: noted. I'll instrument extra logs around kvcache eviction and resume token issuance for next 24h.

elena: scheduling canary today at 2035001280, will report results.

alex: thanks all. tagging this thread INC-2035001 for updates.
